analysis:
Both changed files are documentation-only. No executable source, wire format or cryptographic path changes in the supplied units.

Files examined:
- docs/reference/configuration.md: the visible change is the DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE row (head line 413). It now says the default is `enforce`, only exactly `off` disables it, and `provider.toml` `[backend] prefill_deadline_mode` takes precedence. The same patch also adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES row (head line 414), forwarded to the launchd job. The rest of the configuration.md head text I read (SSD prefix cache keys, TTL ≤1800 s, cache.directory/volume_uuid, DEBUG-only debug key file, ephemeral-key gating) appears unchanged from the base and consistent with the T-041 posture: 30-minute TTL cap, HMAC-keyed names, volume UUID pinning.
- docs/reference/prediction-decision-telemetry.md: the date is bumped and a paragraph is added explaining how the provider charges decode once per batch step and caps MTP rows. It states explicitly that no wire fields change. This adds no new data exposure; it is consistent with the existing allowlisted, bounded telemetry fields (T-058 context).

Security relevance:
- The documented prefill-deadline default flip (off to enforce) is an availability and admission-control behavior change. It is not a confidentiality or integrity control, and the actual source change is not in the supplied evidence. Deadline admission affects only request acceptance, not authorization or encryption.
- I found no threat-model regression. The documentation does not loosen the T-041 TTL, KEK or lookup-tag claims. Several controls described are documented as not forwarded to the LaunchAgent, which keeps installed daemons at their defaults.

Residual questions for integration, outside this batch: whether the code implementing the enforce-by-default change and the AdmissionRateEstimators correction matches these docs, and whether the default-on enforcement could unexpectedly refuse requests (DoS, T-010/T-029 class). The patch excerpt for configuration.md is truncated, so I cannot confirm there are no other changed rows.
